content.comment_body: In my shutters project, I’ve attached supporting information below. I control a shutter depending on temperature changes. If you review the setup, each I1, I2, I3 input has a wiping relay labeled B027, B028, B029, each set to a 2-second delay. There’s logic behind this timing: if the program starts with all inputs off (simulating a power failure during motion) and you switch I1 on within 12 seconds with the relay set to 1 second, failure can occur. A short delay is needed so M1 turns ON briefly, anticipating imminent shutter movement. Failure rules, referenced as FAILURE B084, state that you cannot have M1 STOP, Q2 UP, and Q3 DOWN active at the same time. Initialization, referenced by INITIALISATION B151, disables everything for 12 seconds and then turns Q2 UP until the I1 top input becomes active. Using the cycle menu gives immediate action, but still, why is a 2-second delay necessary? Can someone point out where the trace is missing?

I reviewed your user program with the [product_name] simulator and version [version_no]. B028 (wiping relay), M1, and B084 (OR) behave normally after setting I1 (with I2 and I3 turned off). Eventually, B074 (up-down counter) reaches 1, activating B075 (message text). However, your program is quite extensive, making it hard to grasp all details. Please narrow it down to only relevant sections. For testing on an actual [product_name], I need to know which version you're using. For simulation, a version like [version_no] is sufficient. Are you encountering the issue on your physical [product_name], or solely in the simulator?
